I don't really fight, but that is a bit of an unreasonable expectation to put on others. It's actually caused issues in a some relationships. Kinda funny to have a fight about how we don't fight...

Here are a few tips I try to remind myself. Try to control my emotions so they don't control me. Only I have control of my emotions, no one else. It's my fault, not theirs, if I let my anger get the better of me. With so many emotions to choose from, why choose the toxic ones?

I also like an old proverb or whatever about everyone having two wolves inside us fighting each other. The one that wins is the one we feed. I feed the me I want to win.
What a great proverb, and so true.

These are more general guidelines my wife and I use to keep arguments civil and eliminate many problems before they get to the point of an argument.

Follow the golden rule "Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets." Matt 7:12 when you argue. If you wouldn't want to be called something or yelled at maybe it's best to not do those things yourself.

Try to avoid yelling because that will lead to a communication break down really fast.

No name calling just discuss the issue like the adults you're supposed to be.

Respect boundaries and when someone needs to have a moment let them take it. Sometimes when I am angry about something I would rather wait for a moment to cool off before I discuss it. My wife has the same need sometimes.

Voice concerns as they arise. If something annoys you let them know now because it will build and come out when you argue about something entirely different. A simple argument that would be resolved quickly becomes an ambush as you let the other person have the complete backlog of complaints you have against them and they are completely taken by surprise. Then a minor argument turns into a huge fight.

Resolve any fight before you go to sleep. Going to bed angry will only prolong the ordeal and could lead to deep seeded resentment.

Don't do the silent treatment. If you don't say anything about what is bothering you then it isn't important. I say this because your spouse is most likely not a mindreader and has no idea why you are mad and giving them the silent treatment. It will only lead to an argument that could have been avoided if you were honest from the start. If you feel silly over what annoyed you and realize it shouldn't have, put that as the precursor when you tell them. It will make you feel better and could lead to a good conversation.

Though Your mileage may vary with this advise because my wife and I are pretty out there for the most part.

All great points. Sometimes I have personally found--occasionally mind you, not typically--that going to bed on a fight causes me to wake up with a clear mind and a fresh perspective. Different people have different levels of emotional flux, and at different times.. and some people take longer to mellow out, period. A good night's sleep is the reset button of the brain.
